record.final_answer:
No, there are no published numbers that show the agents can handle 50k lines/s with TLS on.

The only published benchmark is the **Marrowlog 2.4 performance report** (https://marrowlog.example/perf/2026-q2, 2026-06-18). It shows 180,000 lines/s on 1 vCPU at 85% CPU. That figure doesn't match our setup:

| | Their benchmark | Our setup (`README.md`, `config/agent.yaml`) |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | Plain TCP only, TLS never enabled | TLS to the collector (required by end of next quarter) |
| Line size | 200 bytes or less | About 900 bytes (JSON with stack traces) |
| CPU | 1 vCPU | 1 vCPU reserved, same |
| Disk buffer, batching | Off, `batch_lines: 500` | Off, `batch_lines: 500`, same |

The report says outright that TLS and lines over 200 bytes weren't measured. Each of our lines is about 4.5 times longer, so we push roughly 45 MB/s compared with their roughly 36 MB/s, before any encryption cost. The 180k figure can't be scaled down to cover our case.

The maintainers plan to measure TLS in their Q4 report. It isn't out yet: `/perf/2026-q3` and `/perf/2026-q4` both return 404.

If we need an answer before the Q4 report comes out, we'll have to measure it ourselves. That means one agent on 1 vCPU with `tls: true`, fed about 900-byte lines at 50k/s, while we watch CPU use and the backlog.
